s: I'm Maya, and this is Lena.
And today we're talking about travel — the kind of travel that gives you stories for years.
From quiet days on the beach to a full adventure holiday, we'll share our own travel tales and teach you seven wonderful words along the way.
Last summer I finally took the beach holiday I'd been dreaming about for years.
Three whole weeks with nothing but sand, sea, and sunshine.
Which beach did you go to?
A small beach on the west coast.
No crowds, no loud music, just a long stretch of golden sand.
The beach was so quiet in the morning that I almost had it to myself.
What did you do all day on the beach?
I'd read a book in the shade, swim a little, walk along the water.
And in the late afternoon, a soft breeze would come off the sea.
That cool breeze was my favorite part of every day.
There's nothing like an ocean breeze.
It just makes everything feel calm and slow.
One evening the breeze picked up a little, and I sat on the warm sand and watched the waves until the sun went down.
No breeze anywhere else has ever felt that good.
Getting to the beach must have been easy, right?
The airport was packed, of course — airports in summer always are — but my flight landed on time.
An hour after leaving the airport, I was in a taxi, heading for the coast.
Did you stay on the beach the whole time, or did you explore?
One day I rented a bicycle and rode to a tiny fishing town along the coast.
My bicycle was old and a bit rusty, but it was fun.
Riding that bicycle along the cliffs, with the sea below and the breeze in my face — it was lovely.
A bicycle ride by the sea?
And the beach was waiting for you when you got back.
Though the road back to my hotel was incredibly bumpy — a rough, bumpy dirt track through the dunes.
My poor bicycle shook the whole way.
A bumpy ride back to a calm beach.
And that evening, with the breeze coming through my window, I thought: this is what holidays are for.
I swear I could have stayed on that beach forever.
Want words like beach and breeze to stick?

Okay, my turn — and my summer was the complete opposite of quiet.
I went on an adventure holiday in the mountains.
A real adventure holiday: mountain biking, kayaking, the works.
The centerpiece of the whole adventure holiday was the bicycle.
Every morning we'd take a bicycle out on the mountain trails.
My bicycle was a proper mountain bike — thick tires, strong brakes, the works.
I've never been brave enough to ride a bicycle on a real mountain trail.
The first trail was smooth and easy.
But the second one was really bumpy.
One long stretch was so bumpy that my hands went numb.
Bumpy mountain trails are no joke, believe me.
I'd probably get off my bicycle and walk it down a bumpy hill.
Honestly, on the bumpiest part, I almost did exactly that.
But then came the downhill ride — and it was exhilarating.
The wind, the speed, the green valleys below.
I have never felt anything so exhilarating.
So the whole adventure holiday was worth the sore legs?
By day three, riding my bicycle felt natural, even on bumpy forest paths.
And every evening, after an exhilarating day in the mountains, we'd sit by the lake and laugh about it all.
It was the most exhilarating week of my entire year.
And what about the kayaking part of your adventure holiday?
Oh, that was on day four!
The lake looked calm in the morning, but by noon the water got bumpy — little waves everywhere.
Paddling through bumpy water is harder than it looks.
I never thought of water as bumpy.
But crossing that bumpy lake was exhilarating in its own way.
And when I reached the far shore, a cool breeze came through the pine trees, and I just sat there, happy and tired.
Did you feel safe doing all this?
An adventure holiday sounds wonderful, but also a little wild.
We had a fantastic guide, and the company checked every bicycle before we rode.
A good adventure holiday always puts safety first — helmets, life jackets, the works.
I'd never book an adventure holiday without that.
So the only scary part was the bumpy trails?
And honestly, even the bumpy parts became fun by the end.
On the last night, we had dinner on the mountain, and a warm breeze moved through the valley below us.
I looked around at everyone laughing, and I thought: this is what travel should feel like.
Exhilarating, a little bumpy, and completely unforgettable.
Maybe next year I'll trade my beach for an adventure holiday.
What should I know before I book a bicycle trip?
First, expect bumpy roads — pack gloves, your hands will thank you.
And pick a bicycle that actually fits your height.
A bad bicycle will ruin an adventure holiday faster than bad weather.
And do the mountains get a nice breeze, like the coast does?
Up high, the breeze is cool and fresh, and after an exhilarating climb, that breeze feels like a reward.
I'm adding mountains to my list.
But tell me — how do you even pack for an adventure holiday?
My beach packing is easy: swimsuit, book, done.
Packing for an adventure holiday is an adventure in itself.
Sturdy shoes for the bumpy trails, a rain jacket, and layers.
The weather in the mountains changes fast — sunshine one minute, cold breeze the next.
No, the company provides the bicycle — a proper mountain bicycle, already tuned.
Honestly, the hardest part of the whole adventure holiday was the flight home.
Speaking of flights — airport wisdom time.

I have a love-hate relationship with the airport.
The airport is where every adventure begins — and where things go wrong.
My golden rule: get to the airport two hours early for international flights.
My worst airport memory: a delayed flight, then a cancelled connection, and I spent the whole night sleeping on an airport bench.
The airport at three in the morning is a strange, sad place.
Actually — that's good practice for our listeners too: complaining politely at an airport is a real-life English skill.
But here's a nicer airport thought: some airlines let you check a bicycle as luggage.
You can fly into a new city, pick up your bicycle at the airport, and ride straight out into the sunshine.
Airport to beach on two wheels, with the breeze in your hair.
Now that is an exhilarating arrival.
Or skip the airport entirely and take the train!
For shorter trips, I love trains.
No long airport lines, no bumpy bus ride to the airport — you just sit back and watch the countryside.
But trains can't take you across an ocean.
For a real adventure holiday far away, the airport is unavoidable.
My rule: enjoy the journey, whatever it is.
A bumpy road, a long flight, a quiet beach — it's all part of the story.
Another adventure holiday, or a calm beach this time?
A week on the beach, then an adventure holiday in the hills nearby.
So whether your style is a calm beach, a wild adventure holiday, or a bit of both — travel gives you the best stories and the best English practice.
Let's do a quick recap of our seven words.
An adventure holiday — a holiday with exciting, sometimes dangerous activities.
An airport — the place where planes take off and land.
A beach — sandy land next to the sea.
A bicycle — a vehicle with two wheels that you pedal.
A breeze — a gentle, light wind.
Bumpy — not smooth, with many rough parts.
And exhilarating — making you feel very happy, excited, and full of energy.
Try to use all seven today.
Tell a friend about your most exhilarating trip, or your bumpiest bicycle ride!
Practice them in the app, keep listening, and we'll see you tomorrow.
Thanks for listening to Muse English!
